text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Parliament is expected tomorrow to approve the candidature of Vassily Melnik for the post of finance minister. Prime Minister Andris Shkele said that failing to approve the candidature may undermine the stability of the government.
- The public prosecutor's office said it has no evidence of Vassily Melnik having breached the anti-corruption law.
- The Foreign Ministry said it has neither discussed nor would discuss selling the former Soviet naval base at Liepaja to Russia.
- Follwing the attack on the post office van last Saturday, the Ministry of the Interior has started to provide security for post office transport distributing pensions.

- High-ranking police officials kept silent and just smiled as a journalist at a press conference in the Interior Ministry suggested that the future finance minister had been involved in alcohol smuggling.
- Shkele decided to spend his half-year salary (about 2,700 lats) on buying books for rural libraries.
- Compared to 1995, the losses of the Latvian Shipping Company in 1996 more than halved from $51.4 million to $25 million, according to the audit by Coopers & Lybrand.

- Vassily Gyltaychuk, the director of IGE TV, which was banned from broadcasting on the Seventh channel from January 1. He claims Latvian television has been seized by a narrow group of people, representing the leading Latvia's Way party.
